title: Wreck and Trail
premise: Cyrus Brightwater has spent a decade outrunning her mother's legacy—both the fame of the archaeologist who mapped the Vell Range and the grief that made her flee. When a government survey team vanishes near her mother's last, unfinished dig site, Cyrus is the only tracker who can read the ground well enough to find them. Following the trail forces her to retrace her mother's route, confront the truth about why the survey team was really there, and decide what she's willing to pay to survive. She reaches the lost team and exposes the concession scheme that erased them, crossing the range ahead of the snows—not invisible anymore, but finally choosing to stay and claim the inheritance she once abandoned.
about_author: Paloma Amberdale is the pen name of a former trail-crew cook who spent six seasons in the northern ranges before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people who are better at leaving than staying.

chapters.title: The Weight of Staying
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Working a seasonal trail-maintenance contract in the foothills, Cyrus is days from moving on when she hears the survey team is overdue. Her instinct is to leave before anyone asks her for help. Emotional beat: the restless comfort of always having one foot out the door, and the first crack in it.

chapters.title: Gear With No Owners
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. A ranger begs her to at least look at the last known camp. Cyrus finds abandoned equipment arranged too neatly—no panic, no tracks leading out, and a government transit case stenciled with her mother's initials. Emotional beat: dread curdling into reluctant obligation.

chapters.title: What the Ground Remembers
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Reading the site like her mother taught her, Cyrus finds a trail deliberately erased—swept, not scattered. Someone wanted the team unfound. She agrees to track them, telling herself it's for the fee. Emotional beat: the seductive pull of a puzzle only she can solve.

chapters.title: The Concession Papers
chapters.summary: Cyrus and ranger Deputy Okafor, alternating POV. In the county records office, Cyrus learns the survey was a pretext: a mining consortium's permits expire at first snow, and the 'vanished' team was mapping claims her mother once proved should be protected ground. Emotional beat: anger at being handed someone else's war.

chapters.title: Cold Camp
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. First night on the trail alone. Flashbacks surface unbidden—her mother teaching her to read scree, the fight that ended them, the funeral she skipped. Emotional beat: grief she's outrun for a decade finally keeping pace.

chapters.title: The Erased Switchback
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Cyrus finds where the trail was rerouted through a slide chute—a route only someone with her mother's field notes would know. Someone on the survey team had them. Emotional beat: the chilling realization the trail leads into her mother's unfinished business.

chapters.title: A Man in the Talus
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. She finds the first survivor—surveyor Tomas Reyes—trapped with a broken leg in a boulder field, alive because he refused to follow the team leader's order. He tells her the leader, Vess, took the notes and went ahead with a hired guide. Emotional beat: wary trust between two people who owe each other nothing.

chapters.title: Splitting the Load
chapters.summary: Cyrus and Tomas, alternating POV. Cyrus rigs a litter and they move slowly toward the ranger station, arguing about whether to summon help or push on. Tomas reveals Vess was paid to falsify the survey. Emotional beat: the arithmetic of survival—who to save, what to abandon.

chapters.title: Storm Line
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Weather turns early. Cyrus must choose: descend with Tomas and lose the trail, or cache him with supplies and go on alone. She leaves him her tent, a radio, and a guilt she doesn't examine. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal—she pays in company.

chapters.title: Her Mother's Cache
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Sheltering in a cave, Cyrus finds a supply cache her mother stocked years ago—dated after their estrangement, stocked with things only Cyrus would need. Her mother expected her to come here someday. Emotional beat: love arriving too late to be simple.

chapters.title: The Second Grave
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Cyrus finds a cairn with the guide's body beneath it—and Vess's journal page pinned under a stone, half-confession, half-alibi. The guide died in a fall Vess caused or failed to prevent; the notes are gone ahead with him. Emotional beat: horror at how survival can hollow a person out.

chapters.title: Vess
chapters.summary: Cyrus and Vess, alternating POV. Cyrus catches Vess at a river crossing. He's gaunt, half-frozen, still clutching the notes. He claims the team voted to push for the summit claim before the permits lapsed and the mountain killed the rest. Emotional beat: recognition—Vess is what Cyrus becomes if she never stops running.

chapters.title: The Bargain at the Ford
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Vess offers her a share of the claim's finder's fee if she helps him cross and disappears. Cyrus nearly takes it—money, distance, a new name. Emotional beat: temptation, and the moment she understands stopping has always cost less than she feared.

chapters.title: What She Took
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Cyrus takes the notes but not the bargain, and leaves Vess with fire, food, and coordinates for rescue—justice by paperwork, not by mountain. She turns upward alone. Emotional beat: the first choice she's made in years she doesn't want to outrun.

chapters.title: The Ascent
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Alone above the tree line, racing the snow line, Cyrus climbs the route from her mother's notes—each landmark a memory she can't skip. A storm pins her for two days in a snow cave with nothing but the notes and her anger. Emotional beat: stripped down to what inheritance actually means.

chapters.title: The Unfinished Dig
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Cyrus reaches her mother's final site: a sheltered high basin where her mother had documented evidence the consortium's claims were fraudulent—evidence never filed because she died before the season ended. The survey team was sent to destroy or bury it. Emotional beat: her mother wasn't chasing glory; she was standing guard.

chapters.title: Snowfall
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. First true snow begins. Cyrus has hours, not days. She documents the site with the survey team's own equipment, then packs the field records against her chest. Emotional beat: grief and purpose fused into a single forward motion.

chapters.title: The Crossing
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. The descent in whiteout, navigating by memory and her mother's route descriptions, injured, half-blind, refusing to stop because stopping now costs everything. Emotional beat: survival not as escape but as delivery—she is carrying something that matters.

chapters.title: Rescue at the Line
chapters.summary: Cyrus, Okafor, and Tomas, alternating POV. Cyrus walks into the ranger station as the roads close behind her. Tomas made it; Vess was found alive and arrested; the notes and her documentation break the consortium's claims. Emotional beat: the strange lightness of having arrived somewhere on purpose.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. In the inquiry, Cyrus must speak her mother's name, her own history, and everything she buried to stay invisible. The permits are denied; the basin is nominated for protection. Emotional beat: the cost of staying paid in full, and found bearable.

chapters.title: The Inheritance
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Cyrus returns to the basin in spring with a small protection survey crew—and finishes her mother's dig, cataloguing what she left behind. She reads the last page of the field notes: a message addressed to her. Emotional beat: inheritance as a hand held out across time, finally taken.

chapters.title: Where the Trail Ends
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Cyrus signs a lease on the cabin at the trailhead, hangs her mother's compass by the door, and takes a contract that doesn't end at first snow. A ranger asks if she's staying. She says yes. Emotional beat: the adventure complete—not the crossing, but the stopping.
